links.reason: நவைசெய் பிறவிக் கடலகத்துன் பாத கமலந் தொழுவேங்கன் பசையாப் பவிழப் echoes Kural 10's sea of births and feet, but the contrast that the Kural offers a crossing 'from outside' is not in the couplet, and 'answering a known formula' is a guess. The hymn's sense is flagged uncertain.

The verse says he takes no joy (அதுமகிழ்வாயல்லை) yet they keep love; that fits a god without liking (வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை). But the 'reason the worshippers do not need his pleasure' is stated nowhere in the verse, and the other-side gain is generic.

Both are யாரே...அன்றே question-answer hymns on feet and flowers, but neither answers or fulfils the other; 2739 asks who wear his feet, 1245 who rose up. The 'why one worships' lesson is a reading the Tamil does not carry.

The crowd's guesses (புனமயிலே, அன்னமே, பொன்னங்கொம்பே, தாமரைமகளே, அமரர்மகள்) do match Kural 1081's அணங்கு/மயில்/மாதர். But the verse reads as praise, not as lovers' confusion, so the gain that the guesses show 'confusion of love' is not in the Tamil.

Same argument, ஞாலத்தாராண்மை என்னாம் (2284) and ஆண்மையார் கண்ணதம்மா (2300): lovers of women who tremble or flee lack manliness. The claim that it 'serves either army' is not shown by either verse; the link is a repeated taunt, not a distinctive shared image.

எழுமையும் இயைந்து and இம்மை மாறி மறுமை ஆயினும் both reach past this life, but 'ten verses later the hero leaves' is plot outside the Tamil, and 'love granted across births' is the narrator's phrase, not a grant. The qualification rests on an unstated plot.

சாவ நலிந்திடுந் தண்ணீர்ப் பிணி...நஞ்சின் வாவிகள் காட்டலின் and நீருண்ணலுற்றாற் சீப்படு குழம்பதாகி both turn the thirsty's relief into the harm. The pairing shows the same device with different liquids.

1153 is the kings guessing whether the king rages at காலன் or at those who rule ages; Naladiyar 21 (தூற்றப்பட்டார், எஞ்சினார் இல்லை) says kings die. The kings do not say he is 'above their end'; the pairing is only kings and death.

தணப்பறப் பருகும் in 199 recalls பருகியிட்டான் in 190, and the shift from delight to the start of the fall (திரு இழுக்குற்ற) is a fair reading. But the two sit in one scene of the plot, so this is a repeated word more than a distinct link.

The father says தாதையென்றியலுரை தவத்தினெய்தினேன்: he does not ask the Kural's question, and he speaks of his own fatherhood, not of his sons' worth. The note misdescribes the verse, though tapas and sons do link to Kural 70's என்நோற்றான்.

158 has the queen say என்கண் வினையினால் விளைவு கண்டாய், and 143 the king say வினைகளின் விளைவை யாவர் விலக்குநர்; these agree rather than conflict, so tension is the wrong type. That the queen's words are an excuse for her own deed rests on plot not in the Tamil.

In 452 Civakan routs the கானவர் and the herd turns back; in Silappathikaram 12:128-131 the brothers' herds from yesterday's raid fill the yards of the smith and drummer. They are two different raids in different epics, not 'one cattle raid from both ends'.

384 only has the teacher seated under an அம் தளிர்ப் பிண்டி நீழல், a stock setting; the dream's falling tree (223) is a royal emblem, not 'the very tree'. Joining them by the word பிண்டி asks the reader to supply the fulfilment.

அறவாழி வேந்தன்...அடியேத்தி does share அறவாழி and the feet with Kural 8, and reading ஆழி as 'wheel' is a real lexical point. But 2814 is about the groups of five, six and nine, so it gains nothing from the couplet about 'nothing else carries one across'.

மன்னன் கொள்ளின் with the elephant fed in measure against the one that grazes the field gives the prudential reason that Kural 552's கோலொடு நின்றான் இரவு lacks. The note describes both ends accurately and the two gains hold.

2846 gives கூடிய மும்மை as the fire that burns the tree of deeds, and 3064 has Civakan cut the eight karmas (நணிதினெண் வினை) by a துப்பமை சிந்தை: the sermon and its enactment. The link is real and teaches the unity of doctrine and deed.

2741 has கருமக் கடல்கடந்த செல்வன் and his praisers as ஆழிச் செல்வர், an image akin to Kural 10's sea and feet. But the two do not 'disagree': the verse is not offering sovereignty in place of release, and the 'short of the end' gain is not in the Tamil.

Kalittokai 8 ends மன்னவன் புறந்தர வரு விருந்து ஓம்பி...அது மனும் பொருளே, redefining wealth as the guest-feeding household; Kural 81's இல்வாழ்வதெல்லாம் விருந்தோம்பி gives that its purpose. The development into an argument against the journey is real.

37 has the king rage (வெகுண்டுரை) and the ministers settle on something else, after 36's praise. That is the next beat of one scene; 'plot' is read in, and 'telling a rival's merits does not calm a king' is a general moral the Tamil does not teach.

1595 says learning is a துணை in weakness, close to Kural 414's ஒற்கத்தின் ஊற்றாந் துணை. But 'a man of many treatises' failing to be consoled and the mantra returning his wife are not in the verse; the test case is supplied from outside.

556 is the king speaking to வீணாபதி (அரிவை), asking her to be father and mother; it does not charge the merchant. 607's proclamation naming Sitattan (நாய்கன்) as father therefore does not develop that charge, and hiding her birth is not in either verse.

377 is Mokkalan's objection that what stays cannot act (the reply is in the next verse); Kural 331 is the moral error of taking what passes for what lasts. Joining them by நிலை, and the Jain doctrine of substance and mode, is supplied from outside.

1792 is only the maidens' eyes falling on the prince like bees on an elephant; it says nothing of beauty passing. Naladiyar 102 (உருவும் இளமையும்...ஒருவழி நில்லாமை) is about impermanence, so the link is only the shared topic of beauty.

106 has the friend urge (நிறையினைச் சிறைசெய்க) and 110 has her resolve and go, so one character reverses. The two verses do not make incompatible claims; 'pity' and the friend's going to the keeper are read in, and 107-109 intervene.

The patikam line (பன்றி எய்து...பகை நாம் அறக் கொன்ற வாறும்) does join the boar and the enemy's death, but 2177 only proclaims the bride for the boar-shooter and names no enemy. 'Never chiefly about a bride' overreaches: the verse says the shooter becomes her husband.

AK 154's பொய்க்கும் இவ்வூரே and KT 34's மறுப்பத் தேறலர்...இனியது கேட்டின்புறுக do both touch the town's gossip, and the second turns to marriage news. The note's rule that 'the only cure the poets allow is marriage' is a general claim two poems cannot carry.

இலம்பெரிதென இரந்தவர்கட் கேந்திய matches Kural 221's வறியார்க்கொன்று ஈவது, but the verse says nothing of leaving the world or of no return. That is the marker's gloss, so the epic merely illustrates the couplet.

249 says ஊழ்வர அன்னதேனும்...சூழ்ச்சியுட் டோன்றும், and the marker itself holds the sense open. The note builds 'deliberation is where fate takes shape' and a 'limit on its boast' on that reading, whereas Kural 620 says effort sees fate's back; the two are not shown to meet.

1594's threat (தேவிக்குத் தெரியச் செப்புவேன்) and 1595's promise (இனிச் செய்தல் இல்லை) are consecutive beats. 'Who rules in the household' is not in the Tamil, so this is plot sequence with a moral added.

357 has the wives say போவது பொருள் எமக்கும் and bear the tapas with him; it makes no claim about household virtue, so there is no incompatible claim to set against Kural 46's what-gain question. 'Ministers' leaving is not in this verse.

1088 has pots poured over the youth, and 1091 has mountain water and a flower-rain over the bride. Neither verse names 'Vidyadharas from above' or 'kings', nor 'the fire', so the note's contrast of guests is not in the Tamil.

463's women wish பூமியும் புணர்க for the unknown youth, and the patikam's 26 gives his bride and the umbrella and sceptre over the land (செங்கோல்...குடை நிழல் பாய). The blessing is fulfilled in the outcome, which the pair shows.

375 gives அருவினை கழிய நின்ற நெறி through knowledge; 820 gives rite, festival and gifts that put away போர்கெழு களத்துப் பாவம் with grief. The two Jain answers contrast, but 'assigns them by station' is not in either verse.

Both name lust leading to hell: தீவினைப் பறவைத் தோ?நரகத்து and தாங்கா நரகம் தன்னிடை உழப்போர். But 'only ascetics manage it' and Civakan 'simply turning his mind' are read in, and 1633's hell line is corrupt.
ஏமமில் மூதூர் in 24 and சிறையில்லாத மூதூர் in 23 are near-repeated items in one list of 'painful things'. 'Defenders and dwellers' is a gloss; the pair shares a theme without a development.

44 foretells rule, tapas and release; 59 shows the youth mastering learning and elephants under the sage's teaching. That is plot order, and the verse names no step toward release; 'skill as a stage on the way' is read in, and the four things are unnamed.

Both verses use the proverb (தீத்தொட்டாற் சுடுவதன்றே; தீண்டினார் தமைத் தீச் சுடும் மன்னர் தீ), so the shared image is real. But that the hall's fire is the hidden prince is a dramatic reading the Tamil does not state.

408's பழவினை பரிய நோற்பான் (penance wears away deeds) and Tirumanthiram 1527's தன்செயல் அற்றால்...குருவென வந்து are different routes to release, but 408 is a narrative of a teacher leaving, not a claim about grace. Tension would need the epic to deny grace.

1113 is a plain scene of union (கலவியுங் களிப்பும்...மதுவுண்டார்போல்); it takes no view of the daze. Tirumanthiram 1960's விந்து ஒழியா வகை is a yogic teaching about union, so the link is the shared topic only.

நலம்புகழ்ந்தூடல் நீக்கி...புல்லி does fit Kural 1303's புலந்தாரைப் புல்லா விடல், and the order of praise then embrace is true. The 'king must yield' and 'answer owed' gains are not in either text; the epic illustrates the couplet.
899 builds the maiden-city (கன்னி மாநகர் கன்னிக் கியற்றினார்) and 900 has her enter it (கன்னி மாநகரெய்தினள்). It is consecutive plot with a repeated word, not an answer or reversal.

Kural 445 has counsellors as eyes (சூழ்வார்கண் ஆக); 234 has lotus and sun (தாமரை...கதிரினால் விரியும்). The images differ, so same_image does not fit, though both say a king depends on counsel (கண்ணிய புலவரால்). The gains restate the verse.

1251 has the staff-bearer report படையுடைந்திட்டது, and 1255 has the king laugh (நக்கனன்) over one man's bow breaking the army. The answer is plot sequence, and 'a boast' is a reading of an ironic நன்று போர் நமர்களது, with verses between.

400's feeding (பெய் பெய் என்று...விலாப் புடை பெரிதும் வீங்க) does relieve the ascetic's hunger, as Kural 225's பசியை மாற்றுவார் does. But the verse does not show his endurance failing, and 'the boy above the vow' is the marker's gloss, so it is an illustration.

claims.gist: hell-beings enter their great misery through deeds done earlier
those who do penance without desire, attachment or doubt, giving up women, become Indra-like and reach heaven

claims_rejected.why: sense unclear; a conditional about women's glances
narrates the attainment of omniscience; no one states a doctrine
hyperbolic praise of the girl's birth, not a doctrine
an omen shown, not stated as doctrine
a lover's practical inference, not a doctrine

claims.gist: intending to kill even a lifeless effigy brings suffering through births
those who kill without compassion have no destination but hell
calling poison nectar does not make it nectar; a deceiver is not made worthy by wishing
the five-word nectar the Lord taught, taken at death, gains a good state
the stench of hell's pits and pools kills other creatures even a yojana away
gifts to the unrestrained lead to birth on sea-islands, living on the fruit of fate
even Indra-like lords of the gods lose their forms and perish, countless times
knowledge is understanding 'this is the real thing'
faith is clearly discerning that thing
conduct is holding both firmly within oneself
those who unite will part, what rises will fall
the born die and the dead are reborn
the wealth seen is the fruit of past penance; think of penance
going to others' wives brings great suffering; giving up fearful lust is good

claims_rejected.why: too unclear to read as a claim about life and death
